newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says private cargo ports more efficient.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says private cargo ports more efficient.

text.p: Mexico's Communication and Transport Ministry said late on Tuesday that the privatisation process at Veracruz, Altamira and Manzanillo ports has made the sites more efficient.
About 80 percent of the cargo at the container ports is operated by private companies, the ministry said in a statement.
"In addition, with the investments made and with the greater efficiency, in some ports the tariffs are lower than those charged when the state managed them," the ministry said.
Mexico's port privatisation began two years ago, with private companies invited to buy a stake in the ports' assets and bid for operating rights.

"This programme looks to intensify regional economic development and to spur the country's general economic activity...to improve and update infrastructure and achieve a much more competitive atmosphere," the statement said.

The ministry is currently considering a bid for the Ensenada port and will next accept bids for key cargo port Lazaro Cardenas in Michoacan state, a multiple-use, container or liquids port. It said it also hopes to sell off interest in smaller fishing ports to regional firms.
